I was going to complain that opencode triggers compaction a long way short of the end of the context window, which is really annoying (my biggest opencode gripe) with copilot's small context windows, but I double checked [the docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/#compaction) and see a `reserved` setting has been recenty added (0fd6f365be0a) to adjust it! Excellent! People can reduce this to help to lessen this issue somewhat. You have `reserved` defaulting to 20000 tokens which seems quite excessive, does it really sometimes need that much?

### How did I create this master plan?

By a **multitude** of iterations (GLM-5 and Kimi K2.5) -- roughly along the lines of the following prompts:

```
1. Conduct an in-depth research on the science of system promoting -- specifically for coding agents like openCode, Crush, Claude Code etc, and download the relevant papers you found to @papers/. Focus on RCT / meta studies / studies in well-renowned magazines. Important objectives a) High quality coding results b) Avoid token waste / context littering c) LLM steering 

2. Study the downloaded papers very carefully and extract/synthesize a comprehensive and detailed report of guidelines and best practices for system promoting that later we are going to use to a) asses the system prompting of FOSS coding agents and b) improve the system prompts and system prompting architecture of an open source agent

Make sure our report is comprehensive, contains all the relevant science and covers everything and is perfect we need for the next steps. 

—

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
=================

After extensive research under @papers/ on the science of system prompting and extracting the findings into an comprehensive guide book to @papers/SYSTEM_PROMPTING_COMPREHENSIVE_REPORT.md, it is now our plan to craft a detailed and evidence based plan now on how to improve the system prompting architecture and implementation of @opencode/.  

1. As a first step, we want to a) analyze and b) assess the system prompts and system prompting architecture of the leading FOSS coding agents based on our research
2. If we stumble across well formulated system prompts or a stellar system prompting architecture (according to our research), we want to note this down as leading examples and input for our endeavor to improve opencodes system prompting

TASK
====
 
In this directory, I downloaded a list of leading free and open source coding agents:

* cline
* crush
* goose
* kimi-cli
* opencode
* Roo-Code
* continue
* gemini-cli
* kilocode
* mistral-vibe
* qwen-code

For each of the agents

1. Please dive deep into the code base and create an exhaustive understanding of a) the way the agent creates system prompts b) how these system prompts end up looking like and c) the system prompting code architecture 

2. Based on our extensive research in @papers/SYSTEM_PROMPTING_COMPREHENSIVE_REPORT.md asses the a) quality of the system prompts and b) system prompting architecture

3. When analyzing the FOSS agent of a model vendor ( @gemini-cli/ for the Google Models, @kimi-cli/ for the Kimi models, @qwen-code/ for the Qwen models and @mistral-vibe/ for the Mistral models), watch out for specifics we can learn that may be relevant for the model family or individual models of that vendor


Create an extensive report with our finding!
—
Now create and indepth and detailed while iterative plan to incorporate the findings of our research a) @papers/SYSTEM_PROMPTING_COMPREHENSIVE_REPORT.md @papers/ as well as our open source code analysis @FOSS_CODING_AGENTS_SYSTEM_PROMPT_ANALYSIS.md into @opencode/: Each step should be a PRable (aka encapsulated and reviewable) increment
—
Can you please deep dive through the plan @OpenCode_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md and restructure it according to priority.

How to define priority:

1. How much impact will a mechanism have based on evidence of the science in @papers/SYSTEM_PROMPTING_COMPREHENSIVE_REPORT.md @papers/ 
2. How widely is this objective backed by the science  - aka not just a result from based one paper, but can be found several papers in a similar form - and our findings in @FOSS_CODING_AGENTS_SYSTEM_PROMPT_ANALYSIS.md 
3. What is the effort and how much churn will it cause in the code base?
—
Skim @OpenCode_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md and the science in @papers/ for over specifying. Also conduct another science web research. It has been proven that over specification hurts LLM (coding) performance
```

@aspiers The word boundary behaviour does **not** align with that of readline/emacs. 

(the `*` character is used to indicate the position of point in the following examples)

If I have this text:

`MERGED*-branches.md` (the result after first using `alt+u` at the start of the string `merged-branches.md`)

... and then  I strike `alt+u` again, the result is: 

`MERGED-BRANCHES.MD*`

In contrast, striking the same keys in readline/emacs produces:

`MERGED-BRANCHES*.md`

In short, `.` should be a word boundary character.

I work on several projects simultaneously, so the history in one OpenCode session becomes cluttered with the prompt history from my other sessions and I need to hit `UO` a thousand times although it was the last prompt of that session.
